English: 1st tone – high flat, steady high pitch (like singing one high note)
2nd tone – rising, low to high (like asking "what?" in English)
3rd tone – falling then rising, low dip (say it low, then up a little)
4th tone – falling, high to low, sharp (like a firm "No!")
Neutral tone – light, short, no tone mark, unstressed
3rd-tone sandhi: when two 3rd tones meet, the first becomes 2nd tone
b – like p in "spa" (unaspirated, no puff of air)
p – like p in "pop" (aspirated, with puff of air)
h – like h in "hat", but stronger from the throat
j – like j in "jeep", tongue tip behind teeth
x – like sh in "she", tongue tip down
zh – like j in "judge", tongue curled back
ch – like ch in "church", tongue curled back, aspirated
sh – like sh in "shirt", tongue curled back
r – like r in "run", tongue curled back
ü – round your lips for "oo" but say "ee"
